items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: The interviewee discusses the 'king of the Zulu' (Zulu King Rex) as a cultural figure and subject of a song he wrote, but does not describe a personal relationship with a specific individual named 'King'.

ctx.x: And I think he's not too good. He's got cough, he coughs, you know, like this, all the time. Yeah. Yeah. So, yeah, you're good friends with Zui Samson. Oh, yeah, yeah.

I wrote a nice tune for him, you see that tune I gave you yesterday? I wrote that especially for him, you see, he come down here especially to be the king of the Zulu. Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. Oh, man, they had a ball that day, you see, but I couldn't get the number enough on time to get the musicians to rehearse it, to play it, and it was all fucked up so I mean I just withdrew it, you see, but I kept it. But that's the last copy I got because I just burnt all the rest of them up, you know? Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah.…

You can play the melody right off your horn see, I mean then you'll be playing a number written in 1910 and 1912. Oh yeah. Yeah, that's why I used imagination about it you know. I used imagination about it, I mean I can hear you see that. I like the number called the . It's got a beautiful melody man. I hold your majesty in blue, greatest of kings for a day. From far off jungle land you come in all your splendor. To drive a troubled worried city's rules away. Though you'll be gone with the dawn of tomorrow. Back…
